analysis: The code snippet defines a method that loads multiple configuration files using a stream. It first creates a default configuration via ConfigurationModel.defaults(), then maps each file to a ConfigurationModel using TomlUtils.loadConfigurationFile(), and finally merges all models using reduce. The functions called may throw runtime exceptions: defaults() can throw UnsupportedOperationException, IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException, NullPointerException; loadConfigurationFile() can throw FlywayException (runtime, intended to propagate) and internally SecurityException from getAbsolutePath and exists. The stream will propagate any exception thrown within the lambda. All these are runtime exceptions. Since the intended behavior is for load failures to propagate to a higher-level handler (as indicated in the description of FlywayException), and the other exceptions (SecurityException, exceptions from defaults) indicate security restrictions or programming errors that should also propagate, there is no need to catch them within this snippet. Adding a try-catch would either hide important errors or break the intended exception propagation.
